item.title: GovBrief Today #576
item.description: Donald Trump's Department of Homeland Security used a tariff audit form to subpoena a Minneapolis reporter's phone records. In February a federal judge twice refused agents a warrant for Georgia Fort's YouTube account because they could not show she had committed a crime. He also ordered them to tell her if they tried again. Weeks later they sent Google a customs summons that needs no judge's signature. Google refused. T-Mobile got one too and complied, and Fort learned in discovery that the government has six months of her calls and texts. The same summons went after the YouTube records of Democracy Now and Megyn Kelly, a conservative who broke with Trump over the Iran war, and neither faces any charges. The law they used is for checking whether an importer paid the duty on a shipping container. The judge set the conditions for a warrant, so the agents picked a process that bypassed the judge. item.title: The Most Expensive Way to Fucking Die Younger
item.description:
Nothing screams “freedom” quite like spending dramatically more on healthcare while leaving people terrified that one diagnosis, ambulance ride, or hospital stay could financially wreck them. The remarkable achievement of the American healthcare system isn’t merely that it costs so fucking much — it’s that an enormous industry has successfully convinced millions of people that inserting insurers, billing departments, pharmaceutical middlemen and shareholders between patients and medical care somehow represents choice.
Other countries certainly have imperfect healthcare systems. They have waiting lists, shortages, bureaucracy and political fights over funding. But “our system has problems too” isn’t the devastating rebuttal people think it is when the alternative includes receiving a five-figure invoice because your appendix decided to become a fucking emergency. Healthcare shouldn’t be socialism, capitalism, left-wing or right-wing. It should be healthcare.

item.title: 7 YEARS CANCER FREE TODAY! (And Album Reveal)
item.description:
Almost everyone here knows about my journey with vision loss (link below for those who don’t) but I’ve never really spoken much on here about my battle with thyroid cancer. In 2014 we were taking care of some kids who were in a god awful situation. Even though they’re both basically grown now, it still kills me inside to think about the horrid abuse these babies suffered and the conditions they had to live in. Their dad had just gotten out of jail and was fighting so hard to get his life together to take his kids from their wretched mom and step dad. Due to the fact they were so dirty and uncared for they had lice. I got them so bad we had to shave my head. I’d always wanted a Mohawk for YEARS (l I started asking for one at like 10) but my gramma refused because “Mohawks were for boys” so I didn’t care, I was all for it. But then we noticed my hair was falling out in sporadic patches my mom called “cow spots” because of how irregular they were. They were very sore around the outside but where the actual hair was gone didn’t hurt. She took me to my PCP and she didn’t run any tests etc she walked in, looked at my head and said “Eh it looks like it grows back. Go to Walmart and get Rogaine for women, IF you can afford it..” needless to say I never saw her again. We went directly across the street to another doctor. My first appointment he took one look at me as he walked in, immediately started asking a series of questions and before he’d even ran any tests he said “I don’t know HOW NO ONE has told you this, but you’ve been sick for a very long time from the way it seems…” he ran a series of blood tests and my T3 and T4 levels were off the charts among other issues. The next day I was laying down as a woman sat there trying to hid the shocked look on her face as she did an ultrasound of my thyroid and it looked like a whole weird alien world with a bunch of tumors and cysts seemingly connected by these stringy little connections in between each one. Over the 5 years it took between diagnosis and safe(ish) removal, we tried many different medications and hormones, I had 3 different endocrinologists because they all kept quitting their places of work and I’ve not had one since my surgery, I was told radiation would take my remaining vision only to be told that wasn’t true very late down the road. Out of everything, no matter what Im being treated for, I’ve learned to just keep asking questions and always get a second, third or even fourth opinion if something doesn’t feel right or you’re not being taken seriously or in my case, if your main medical team can’t come to an agreement on how to even treat you for the longest time. Eventually my heart rate and thyroid swelling was brought down to a level where they finally felt comfortable performing surgery. I still bled way more than expected and they damaged my vagus nerve and right vocal cord in the process. But here I am 7 years later and to say it’s been a wild journey is definitely an understatement. Experiencing what it’s like to go from everything being overactive and out of wack to not having such an important organ and the impacts that has on your body when Im not able to get my meds either due to not being able to pay for them sometimes even with GoodRX or because they keep being delayed like they were recently. But not even a year after surgery I started releasing instrumentals and I got to be in Lucia Cifarelli (KMFDM) music video for “Girls Like Me” that came out during COVID. Outside of playing piano before taking up the harp, I had never written music, had absolutely NO CLUE what I was doing but now I’ve got over 70 songs coming out with a new Dungeons and Dragons album releasing in November. What a wild ride and I wonder what else will happen in another 7 years.
This is the best mockup I’ve been able to come up with for my album until the prints are ordered. My Kickstarter has just over 55 hours left at the time of posting and Im $95 away from my stretch goal! https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/sursie/echoes-of-the-forgotten-realms-join-the-adventure
